version.note: The opened score supplies two soprano, alto, tenor and bass parts, without instruments. Neither the exact edition used by the choir nor its performance transposition is established.

publication.note: Publication date, not a guessed composition year.

text.value: Giovanni Battista Guarini, adapted from Il pastor fido, Act I, scene 1
text.note: LiederNet identifies lines 175–186 and distinguishes Monteverdi’s adapted text. Public prose paraphrases the imagery; no copyrighted modern translation or exact timed syllable is supplied.

completeness.value: Whole nominated Tudor Consort madrigal track
completeness.note: The published concert track is retained intact, including its quiet tail. It is not grouped as a multi-movement set merely because it appears in Book IV or on an album.

scoreEdition.value: Daniel Van Gilst, 2019, CC0, four-page SSATB score
scoreEdition.note: The complete score was opened and viewed. This modern engraving is dedicated to the public domain under CC0. Its transposition is not used to identify the choir’s sounding key or pitch standard.

performers.note: The track description and Carey’s album notes agree. Five written parts do not establish five individual singers, and no instrumental players are credited.

date.note: The track names the Ordizia concert; the album’s first-person liner notes explicitly date it to Wednesday 2 November 2005. The 19 August 2010 date on FMA and Commons is an online release, not the recording session.

place.note: The track and album notes name the venue. The later Rome concert and 2006 New Zealand recording described elsewhere in the same album notes belong to different tracks.

label.note: The album was prepared for the Tudor Consort’s twentieth anniversary, but no original imprint is named. FMA and Commons are access repositories.

catalogue.note: No commercial catalogue number is supplied.

matrixTakeSides.note: The notes refer to a disc but supply no matrix, mastering identifier or take number.

album.note: A mixed concert anthology, with different sessions explicitly distinguished in the liner notes.

credits.value: Timothy Hurd, producer and engineer; Commons import by ComputerHotline
credits.note: Hurd is explicitly credited at album level. The Commons uploader is not presented as the original engineer.

date.note: The 2005 concert date, 2010 FMA release and 11 April 2020 Commons upload do not establish a mastering or transfer date.

processing.value: FMA MP3 source converted to Ogg for Commons; Wikimedia MP3 access derivative
processing.note: Original recording medium, microphones, editing and equalisation settings are not supplied. No further processing or audio trim is introduced here.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative of the Commons Ogg import from FMA

composition.value: Public-domain 1603 madrigal; inspected engraving dedicated under CC0
composition.note: Historical composition rights and Van Gilst’s engraving status are separate from the Tudor Consort’s sound recording rights.

recording.note: The external FMA track was opened directly and explicitly licenses this human choral performance under CC BY 3.0, without a NonCommercial condition. Commons contains a 2024 review template referring anomalously to a Flickr image; that text is not relied upon as verification of an FMA recording. The actual FMA recording page supplies independent evidence.

rights.creditLine: Monteverdi, Quel augellin che canta, SV 87; The Tudor Consort, directed by Alastair Carey. Recorded live, Parroquial Church, Ordizia, Spain, 2 November 2005. Timothy Hurd, producer and engineer. Source: The Tudor Consort / Free Music Archive; Commons import by ComputerHotline. Recording CC BY 3.0; transcoded access copy, no new editorial audio cut.

editorial.timing: audio.mjs analyze completed before annotation; cache/analysis/origins-monteverdi-quel-augellin.txt was read. Broad score-proportion joins use measured boundaries near 0:40 and 1:26, not exact phrase or word alignment. Four 30-second-spaced cues include two musical and two contextual observations under the short-work exception.
editorial.orchestra: One chorus timeline entry represents the score’s five vocal parts. Its note explicitly distinguishes the upper-trio opening from later fuller writing without fabricating entry times or claiming that all five parts sing continuously.
